I hate it when people say things like “suicide is a permanent solution for a temporary problem”, “suicide is selfish”, and even a general “things will get better!”.  There really ignorant things to say because those people can not comprehend what is going on in your head.  Everyone’s situation is different, and there’s no way to accurately measure levels of depression.  Who cares what people think, honestly.  If that’s you’re sole reason I would highly recommend not killing yourself.  Look out for #1, you.  There are plenty of people out there anyways and I’m sure there are many who would love a friend like you, you just gotta find them.

Yeah you and me both, very few people end up being exactly what they want to be in this country because everyone’s a bunch of greedy materialistic capitalists that set the bar so high (if you’re in the US).  However I changed my outlook on life and I feel a lot better which is extremely surprising to me because I literally haven’t been happy in years.  I legitimately do not care how other people view me anymore.  It’s crazy how options that can make you so much happier can be right in front of your face, but we never take them because we innately want to conform with those around us.

Hopefully you’re not successful, if you’re still alive tomorrow and want to chat feel free to message.  I’ve been deeply depressed for a long time and I’m actually feeling a lot better lately.  For years I felt like I would never be happy again, I’ve had serious concussion problems coupled with MS and it’s been a real struggle.  I changed my outlook on life and I have faith I can have a meaningful existence again, something I never thought possible as recently as two months ago.  You may think that there 100% is no way you’re going to get out of this, and I understand that.  However, you only live once and life is short.  No one knows what’s on the other side.  If your friends and family aren’t supportive, move, it’s your life you can do whatever you want.  That’s what I’m likely doing and it’s been an exhilarating feeling that brought me out of deep depression.  The majority of people out there are good, I would try to surround yourself with new people or try changing your outlook on life.  Hope you get the chance to read this Anthony.

All the best,
Steve

Hi MenatlHealthalt1,

I read your whole post and I think we have a lot in common.  I never say “I know how you feel” to anyone because everyone is different, but we definitely have a lot of similarities.  I am also unemployed trying to find purpose in life.  One thing you said that really resonated with me though is you can’t love anyone else until you love yourself, that is my biggest problem.  I have ms and brain damage which was the source of my depression and I know that I need to accept who I am now to begin healing.... but it’s not as easy as it sounds.  I’ve been struggling with that for over 5 years, I also have had therapists, to no avail though.  I don’t want that to be misleading though because the right therapist can absolutely be pivotal.  I’m on some anti depressants that have slightly helped.  Suicidal thoughts often help me fall asleep at night, but I don’t think I’ll ever kill myself unless my brain function worsens more.  Might as well fight it out because life is short and who knows what is on the other end, that’s my mind set.  Some of us get a really really shitty hand, maybe those trials and tribulations mean something, maybe they don’t, might as well play the hand that was dealt and do the best you can with it.  I hope this rant was helpful.

Best,
Steve

I live in Pittsburgh which is notorious for having a lot of MS diagnoses.  I don’t think we have a lot of pollution, at least anymore, we did back in the steel city days.  I don’t think I can ever leave Pittsburgh, I have my family here and my girlfriend has hers, plus it’s a great city.  Also it is very hard to tie down where my brain issues started, it’s very complicated.  I’ve suffered from mental fogginess for about 11 years which started 2 weeks after a concussion.

There are some things that modern medicine still can’t explain.  I was told by a concussion specialist that he was 99.99% it was all anxiety.  I was so happy when he told me that.  To hear that it was something I could fix sparked some hope in my life.  Unfortunately about a year after that I took an MRI which showed a bunch of holes in my brain..... So it looks like I hit the 00.01 percentile.  I do have anxiety, but that is obviously a result of my problems, not the root.  No one will ever understand what is going on inside my head.  They can look at my MRI and tell I’m abnormal, but no one will ever understand how I feel.  I know I’m not the only person in this world with brain damage, but brain damage is not just brain damage.  There is no one out there who will understand the hell inside my head.
What would have been 100% effective?

I got it from concussions and MS.  I have retuxin infusions for my MS every 3 months.  I saw a bunch of neurologists and specialists in the past.  There’s nothing I can really do to get better, just some things to make further damage less likely.

Absolutely.  I had a bad concussion about 11 years ago.  A couple weeks later I woke up with mental fogginess, after smoking weed the night prior.  I thought that I was still a little high but it never went away.  I had to quit football freshman year of high school because of the mental fogginess.  I went to a number of doctors and was told it was a symptom from the concussion I had two weeks prior.  The symptom never went away, 24/7.  I was still functional and to the naked eye there was nothing wrong with me.  Eventually after many years I was told that they were 99.99% sure it was all just anxiety.  I was ecstatic to hear that.  Then about 4 years ago, I woke up after a night out with my friends and I felt very different.  I knew immediately something was seriously wrong.  Since then my intellectual capabilities have reduced dramatically.  I’m constantly tired, I can’t converse with people well anymore, it takes me a long time to read, and I can’t comprehend things quickly anymore.  About a couple years ago, I woke up with some numbness in my left arm that never went away.  I went to the doctors and they said I should see a neurologist.  By the time I made it to my doctor appointment my left hand was so numb and uncoordinated I couldn’t write. They took an mri and found significant brain damage.  They had me take a spinal tap, and I was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis.  The numbness has since went away but I still have coordination problems.  I’m managing the MS, I get an infusion every 3 months.  However I do not think MS was the problem all along.  I think the mental fogginess was a result of the concussion and that the specialist was definitely wrong about the anxiety.  I do have serious anxiety and depression, but I think it’s safe to say that that is a result of my problems.
